title: Web Application Development
description: A practical course in building web applications: web development concepts, website design, UI/UX and responsive design, client-server architecture and tools, client-side programming with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, server-side programming with PHP, object-oriented PHP, and database-driven applications with MySQL, cookies and sessions. Built from B. I. Dahunsi's IFT 302 lessons, the course content document and the PHP lecture slides.

topics.title: Introduction to Web Development
topics.summary: Web development is designing, building, deploying and maintaining websites and web applications. The Web, invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989, evolved from the read-only Web 1.0 to the read-write Web 2.0 and the semantic Web 3.0. Websites are static or dynamic, frameworks speed up development, and client-side and server-side technologies share the work.
subtopics: Website versus web application; static and dynamic sites
Client-side, server-side and the development lifecycle

topics.title: Website Design, UI/UX and Responsive Design
topics.summary: Website design is planning and arranging content to be attractive, functional, user-friendly and accessible. Its principles are simplicity, consistency, visual hierarchy, balance, contrast, white space, accessibility and performance. UI covers what users interact with and UX the overall experience, and responsive design adapts a site to every screen size.
subtopics: Responsive web design and media queries

topics.title: Web Architecture and Development Tools
topics.summary: Web architecture is the structure of the components that deliver web applications. In client-server architecture, clients such as browsers request resources and servers such as Apache provide them over HTTP. Developers use a code editor, browser tools, a local server package such as XAMPP, package managers, Git for version control and MySQL for data.

topics.title: Client-side Programming
topics.summary: Client-side programming runs on the user's device, inside the browser. HTML structures the page with tags, CSS controls appearance and layout, and JavaScript adds interactivity with variables, operators, conditions, loops, functions, DOM manipulation, events and form validation.
subtopics: Control flow, functions and the DOM

topics.title: Server-side Programming with PHP
topics.summary: Server-side programming runs on the web server to receive requests, apply business rules, talk to databases and build dynamic pages. PHP, the Hypertext Preprocessor, runs on the server and sends only its output to the browser. Students set up XAMPP and use PHP variables, constants, data types, operators, conditions, loops, functions, arrays, strings and form data.
subtopics: Client-side versus server-side: a login example
What PHP is and why it is used
Control structures, functions, arrays and forms

topics.title: Object-Oriented Programming in PHP
topics.summary: PHP OOP organises code into classes and objects with properties and methods. It covers $this, instanceof, constructors and destructors, the public, protected and private access modifiers, inheritance with extends, method overriding, final, class constants, abstract classes, interfaces, traits, static members and namespaces.

topics.title: Database-Driven Applications, Cookies and Sessions
topics.summary: A database-driven web application uses PHP to send SQL to MySQL and build responses, implementing CRUD with prepared statements and escaping output with htmlspecialchars. Because HTTP is stateless, applications keep state with cookies stored in the browser and sessions stored on the server, secured with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and session ID regeneration.
subtopics: Session security: fixation, hijacking and cookie flags
